_comment: Hand-written CAPS-aligned seed list for lesson Level 0 topic selection.
No machine-readable CAPS pacing data exists in the workspace yet — the
product docs list 'CAPS curriculum pacing' as an unbuilt feature
the interim source of truth for which subject/grade/topic/subtopic
combinations the factory may open lesson jobs for. Replace or extend it
when a real CAPS pacing source lands.
Field names follow the Prompt Template in agent/replay/docs/supacharge-tech.md
§4: Subject, Grade, Topic, Subtopic, Example problem, Tutor, Prior knowledge.
tutor is optional — when omitted, Level 1 recommends one
(Grandmaster — formal | Big John — simplistic, lower grade logic).
Launch scope per supacharge-tech.md §5 Phase 0: Grade 12 Maths first,
plus the Grade 11 quadratics entries used as the pipeline's worked example.

entries.subject: Maths
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows multiplication, basic algebra

entries.subject: Maths
entries.prior_knowledge: Student can factorise simple quadratics and work with surds

entries.subject: Maths
entries.prior_knowledge: Student can expand brackets and factorise perfect squares

entries.subject: Maths
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows multiplication, basic algebra

entries.subject: Maths
entries.example_problem: Find the 20th term of 3; 7; 11; ...
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows Grade 11 number patterns and linear expressions

entries.subject: Maths
entries.example_problem: Find the 10th term of 2; 6; 18; ...
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows arithmetic sequences and exponents

entries.subject: Physical Sciences
entries.example_problem: A 5 kg crate on a frictionless horizontal surface is pulled by a horizontal force of 20 N. Calculate its acceleration.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows forces as vectors, mass, and basic algebra

entries.subject: Physical Sciences
entries.example_problem: Calculate the mass of CO₂ produced when 8 g of CH₄ burns completely in excess oxygen.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student can balance chemical equations and knows the mole concept

entries.subject: Physical Sciences
entries.example_problem: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. Calculate the total current supplied by the battery.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows Ohm's law and series circuits

entries.subject: Physical Sciences
entries.example_problem: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 5 m. Use conservation of mechanical energy to calculate its speed just before it strikes the ground.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows kinetic and gravitational potential energy

entries.subject: Physical Sciences
entries.example_problem: Calculate the pH of a 0,01 mol·dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid solution.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows concentration, strong vs weak acids, and logarithms

entries.subject: Physical Sciences
entries.example_problem: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, the equilibrium concentrations are N₂ 0,20; H₂ 0,30 and NH₃ 0,60 mol·dm⁻³. Calculate Kc.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows reversible reactions and concentration

entries.subject: Economics
entries.example_problem: Show on one graph how an increase in consumer income shifts the demand curve for beef, and identify the new equilibrium price and quantity.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows the demand curve, the supply curve, and how to read a graph

entries.subject: Economics
entries.example_problem: The price of a product rises from R10 to R12 and quantity demanded falls from 100 to 80 units. Calculate the price elasticity of demand and classify it.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows demand and supply and percentage change calculations

entries.subject: Economics
entries.example_problem: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0,75, calculate the multiplier and the total change in national income resulting from a R100 million injection.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows the circular flow model, injections and leakages

entries.subject: Economics
entries.example_problem: Calculate the inflation rate if the consumer price index rises from 120 to 126 over one year.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows index numbers and percentage change

entries.subject: Economics
entries.example_problem: Draw the equilibrium position of an individual firm earning economic profit under perfect competition, and explain the long-run adjustment to normal profit.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows revenue and cost curves and market structures

entries.subject: Geography
entries.example_problem: Calculate the average gradient between trig beacon 251 (1 200 m) and a spot height of 900 m that are 4,5 km apart on a 1:50 000 topographic map.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student can read contour lines and convert between map units

entries.subject: Geography
entries.example_problem: The distance between two points on a 1:50 000 topographic map is 8,6 cm. Calculate the real distance in kilometres.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows ratio scale and metric unit conversions

entries.subject: Geography
entries.example_problem: Describe the stages in the development of a mid-latitude cyclone and explain its influence on Western Cape winter weather.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows air pressure, fronts, and global wind circulation

entries.subject: Geography
entries.example_problem: Differentiate between a graded and an ungraded river profile, and explain river rejuvenation using a labelled diagram.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows drainage basins and fluvial erosion and deposition

entries.subject: Geography
entries.example_problem: Explain the tri-cellular model of global air circulation and account for the location of the world's major pressure belts.
entries.prior_knowledge: Student knows insolation, air pressure, and the Coriolis effect
